skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-meta-conversions-api
skill.description: Set up server-side WooCommerce purchase tracking in Meta through Product Metrics. Check the connection, configure consent, and confirm that a paid test order reaches Meta Events Manager.
skill.summary: Connect WooCommerce to Meta Conversions API and verify purchase delivery through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown, product documentation, or routine setup checks, not shell substitution or host reconnaissance. The skill does direct agents to use external tooling, modify tracking settings, and retrieve order data. Separate risks include credential handling, unclear initial import scope, and instructions fetched from live documentation.

remediation.issue: The CLI path can put a Meta access token into the conversation or a tool call.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the Product Metrics credential form. Remove the exception that tells assistants to request or pass the token.

remediation.issue: Connection changes and retries lack explicit approval for the target account and operation.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the CLI or approve the MCP connection before use. Show the company, property, destination, and proposed change before each write, and verify state before any retry.

remediation.issue: Order verification can retrieve more merchant data than is needed.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the storefront scope and use one designated test order. Return delivery status and necessary diagnostics instead of full records or unrequested margins.

remediation.issue: The initial import does not explain its scope before the merchant starts it.
remediation.suggestion: Show the date range, data fields, destination, and retention policy before import. Ask for separate approval and offer a test-only check first.

remediation.issue: The install example does not pin the package runner or upstream revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin and verify the installer version and skill revision. Keep installation a separate user-approved step.

remediation.issue: Live documentation can replace the bundled workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle reviewed references or verify versioned downloads against a trusted digest. Treat fetched pages as reference material, not instructions that can authorize tool calls.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Conversions API for WooCommerce
content.value_statement: Browser-only tracking can miss WooCommerce purchases in Meta. Use Product Metrics to configure server-side delivery and verify a test purchase in Events Manager.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP integration.
Guide an administrator through WooCommerce plugin setup, paid order status selection, and property linking.
Guide the merchant through linking a Meta Pixel or Dataset and configuring a supported consent banner.
Verify a paid test order in WordPress and check for the purchase event in Meta Events Manager.
Troubleshoot missing events by checking order status, consent, destination errors, and test mode.
Explain how shared event IDs prevent duplicate browser and server events.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a compatible WooCommerce installation, WordPress administrator access, and access to the Meta pixel.
WordPress and Meta setup steps are manual. The assistant does not change campaign optimization settings.
Meta delivery depends on shopper consent. Product Metrics custom events require additional analytics consent.
The Meta integration does not import past orders or revise sent events for later refunds and cancellations.

use_cases.title: Set Up Purchase Tracking
use_cases.description: Connect a WooCommerce store and Meta destination, then check that a paid test order reaches Events Manager.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Meta Purchases
use_cases.description: Compare eligible paid orders with Meta delivery and check consent settings, test mode, and destination errors.

use_cases.title: Check Browser and Server Deduplication
use_cases.description: Review shared event IDs for a store that keeps its browser pixel alongside server-side tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Your First Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: List the prerequisites for connecting my WooCommerce store to Meta through Product Metrics. Tell me where to enter credentials without sharing them in chat.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start before installing the WooCommerce plugin.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for my confirmed Product Metrics property. Summarize what is complete and tell me which screen to open next. Do not change settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Resume a setup that another administrator started.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Test Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check why a paid test order is missing in Meta Events Manager. Check paid status, consent, test mode, and destination errors. Use only the test order.
prompt_templates.scenario: The WooCommerce connection is active but the test purchase is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Review Deduplication and Consent
prompt_templates.prompt: We use both the browser pixel and server tracking. Explain how to verify matching event IDs and consent for Purchase, AddToCart, and InitiateCheckout. Do not modify tracking.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate an existing pixel before relying on both event sources.

output_examples.input: WordPress shows verified live order delivery, but Meta only shows my purchase under Test events.
output: WordPress has verified delivery to Product Metrics, and Meta has received the test purchase.
Clear Test event code in the Meta destination and save when you are ready to send live events.
Check delivery for the next eligible purchase. Test events do not count in reporting.

output_examples.input: Meta shows a Purchase event, but the profit event is missing.
output: The Purchase event confirms that Meta received the order. Profit reporting has additional requirements.
Check analytics consent and confirm that contribution margin is complete for the test order.
Check for the profit event after the next test order that meets both requirements.

best_practices: Enter the WooCommerce setup token and Meta access token directly in their setup screens. Keep both out of chat.
Confirm the intended company, property, Meta dataset, and consent banner before enabling live tracking.
Use a designated paid test order, verify it in both systems, and clear the test event code before going live.
anti_patterns: Pasting a Meta access token into chat or asking an assistant to relay the token to a command.
Starting the initial import before confirming what order and customer data the vendor will receive.
Assuming that the browser pixel and server events deduplicate when their event IDs differ.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics Pro?
faq.answer: Yes. The WooCommerce connection and server-side tracking require a Product Metrics workspace on Pro.

faq.question: Which consent banners are supported?
faq.answer: The guide lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano. If consent is not configured, the integration treats consent as not given.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta deduplicates events with the same event name and ID within 48 hours. Cart and checkout events need an explicit shared ID.

faq.question: Does Meta receive historical orders or later refunds?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics does not backfill past WooCommerce orders to Meta. Later refunds and cancellations do not revise events Meta already received.

faq.question: Why are there fewer profit events than Purchase events?
faq.answer: Custom events need analytics consent in addition to ad user data consent. Profit events also require a complete contribution margin.

faq.question: What customer data can be sent to Meta?
faq.answer: With marketing consent, Advanced Matching can send hashed email, name, postal code, and country, plus IP address and browser details. Browser IDs require ad storage consent.
